title: Implement equals() and hashCode() correctly for a custom class, then verify it behaves properly in a HashSet
hint: Override both using the same significant fields (Objects.equals and Objects.hash), then add duplicates to a HashSet and confirm only one stays.

title: Write your own immutable class with a mutable field (e.g., a List), including defensive copying in the constructor and accessor
hint: Make the class final with private final fields, copy the list in the constructor with List.copyOf or new ArrayList, and return an unmodifiable view or copy from the getter.

title: Convert a traditional POJO with a builder into a Java Record, and discuss what's gained/lost
hint: A record gives final fields, accessors, equals, hashCode and toString automatically; use a compact constructor for validation, but note records cannot extend classes or be mutable.

title: Write a generic Pair<A, B> or Stack<T> class, and a generic method with a bounded type parameter (<T extends Comparable<T>>)
hint: Declare the class with type parameters like Pair<A,B>, and write static <T extends Comparable<T>> T max(T a, T b) using compareTo for the bound.

title: Implement the Builder pattern for a class with many optional constructor parameters
hint: Create a static nested Builder with setter-style methods returning this, plus a build() method that calls a private constructor taking the builder.

title: Sort a Map by key and by value (ascending and descending), using both streams and a comparator
hint: Stream map.entrySet() sorted with Map.Entry.comparingByKey() or comparingByValue(), optionally reversed, collecting into a LinkedHashMap to preserve order; or use a TreeMap.

title: Write a thread-safe Singleton class, and show how to break and then protect it from reflection and serialization
hint: Use an enum or a private constructor with a volatile double-checked instance; guard reflection by throwing if instance exists, and serialization with readResolve().
